key_insight: VGGT-Edit enables native, feed-forward 3D scene edits by predicting a residual field that modifies a base neural scene representation in one pass, producing multi-view-consistent edits without per-view 2D lifting. This yields fast, interactive 3D editing while preserving geometry and appearance coherence.
problem_solved: Existing generalizable feed-forward 3D reconstructions are difficult to edit interactively: most editing pipelines operate per-view (2D lifting), causing inconsistency across views, high latency, and limited responsiveness to dynamic instructions.
method: Represent scenes with a prebuilt base neural field and learn a compact residual field that encodes edit delta for geometry and appearance.
Predict the residual field in a single feed-forward pass conditioned on user input (masks/text/instruction) and fuse it with the base field to produce the edited scene.
Render the updated neural field directly to obtain multi-view-consistent results, avoiding per-view optimization or lifting steps.
impact: Delivers fast, consistent 3D edits suitable for interactive tools (AR/VR, game content creation, rapid prototyping) and reduces computation compared to iterative per-view methods, making neural 3D editing practical for real-time applications.

paper_title: VGGT-Edit: Feed-forward Native 3D Scene Editing with Residual Field Prediction
paper_authors: Kaixin Zhu, Yiwen Tang, Yifan Yang, Renrui Zhang, Bohan Zeng
